newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS - Phoenix to resist Icopal bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Phoenix to resist Icopal bid.

text.p: A three-way fight to control Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors took an unexpected turn on Friday when a fourth suitor entered the fray.
But Phoenix management vowed to resist Icopal plans to make an offer and said it would sell its own holdings to its favoured bidder, Norway's Rieber and Son, if need be.

"Icopal's management had earlier let it be understood that it did not intend to bid for Phoenix Contractors and the board therefore regards today's statement as hostile," Phoenix chairman Henry Petersen said in a statement.
"The board has authorised the chairman to offer Phoenix Contractors' holdings of its own shares to Rieber and Son if neccessary," he added.
Phoenix was noted last month as holding 2.8 percent of its own equity and 10.1 percent of voting stock.
Rieber, the highest of three bidders so far with an offer of 820 million Danish crowns, said on Thursday that it had built up a stake of 16.5 percent and had 17.4 percent of the votes.
Also bidding for Phoenix is heavyweight Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos which says it will not raise its offer of 808 million crowns.
It nevertheless says that it does not consider itself out of the race.

Superfos is the favoured suitor of some of Phoenix's biggest institutional investors, such as pension fund ATP which holds around 10 percent. The fund also has a 12.6 percent stake in Superfos and close to 14.0 percent in Icopal.
Icopal, which on Friday said it was preparing a generous offer for Phoenix, denied rumours that it planned a takeover in alliance with Superfos.
"We would not come limping in so late if we had a deal with Superfos," managing director Hans C. Andreasen told Reuters.
He said he was joining the battle in an attempt to keep Phoenix in Danish hands.
Another suitor, Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen said last week that it would not raise its offer of 776 million crowns.
The deadline for offers is currently March 7 but would be extended for four weeks from the date of an Icopal bid.

Phoenix's Petersen said that the takeover struggle, launched by Rieber on January 15, had already gone on long enough and further complications would heighten staff insecurity and jeopardise the firm's ability to do business.

The most-traded Phoenix C-share closed up 10 Danish crowns at 675 on Friday. Rieber slipped four Norwegian crowns to 231, Superfos was up 13 Danish crowns to 788 and Icopal rose 30 Danish crowns to 1,550.
